questions.stem: The existence of more than 50000 different strains of rice in India is an example of
questions.explanation: Genetic diversity is variation within a species. The many strains of rice, like the mango varieties of India, differ in their genes and are examples of diversity at the genetic level. Species diversity compares different species.

optionRationale.1: Species diversity is variation among species in a region.
optionRationale.2: Ecological diversity is variation among ecosystems.
optionRationale.4: Beta diversity is diversity between communities, not within a species.

questions.stem: Parthenium (carrot grass), Lantana and water hyacinth in India are examples of
questions.explanation: These plants were introduced from other regions of the world and spread aggressively, harming the native species around them. Alien invasive species are therefore a major cause of biodiversity loss.

optionRationale.1: Endemic species are restricted to one region.
optionRationale.3: Keystone species are native species with critical ecological roles.
optionRationale.4: These plants are abundant, not extinct.

questions.stem: Among the animal species described so far, the largest group is
questions.explanation: Insects make up the greatest number of described animal species, far more than all the vertebrates together. The vertebrate groups such as mammals, fishes and amphibians have relatively few species by comparison.

optionRationale.2: Mammals have only a few thousand species.
optionRationale.3: Fishes are numerous but fewer than insects.
optionRationale.4: Amphibians have far fewer species than insects.

questions.objective: Recall the most species-rich animal group

questions.stem: Conserving the Amazon rainforest because it produces a large share of the earth's oxygen through photosynthesis is an example of the
questions.explanation: The broadly utilitarian argument values biodiversity for ecosystem services such as oxygen release, pollination and aesthetic pleasure. The Amazon forest, producing about 20 per cent of the earth's oxygen, is the standard example.

optionRationale.1: Narrowly utilitarian values are direct products such as food, firewood and drugs.
optionRationale.2: The ethical argument is that every species has intrinsic value.
optionRationale.3: Bioprospecting is the search for economically useful products and is part of the narrow argument.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a biodiversity hotspot found in India?
options: Cape Floristic region of South Africa
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats and Sri Lanka form one of the hotspots that include parts of India, along with the Indo-Burma and Himalaya regions. The other options are hotspots of Africa and South America.

optionRationale.1: This hotspot lies in South Africa.
optionRationale.3: Madagascar is a hotspot, but it lies off Africa.
optionRationale.4: These forests are in South America.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of ex situ conservation?
questions.explanation: Ex situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, in places such as zoological parks, botanical gardens and seed banks. Biosphere reserves, national parks and sacred groves protect species in their natural habitats.

optionRationale.2: Biosphere reserves protect species in their natural habitat.
optionRationale.3: National parks are in situ methods.
optionRationale.4: Sacred groves are in situ and community-based.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species-area relationship S = C A^Z with Z = 0.5, the area increases 36 times. Species richness will increase by a factor of
questions.explanation: With S proportional to A^Z, the new richness is 36 raised to the power 0.5 times the old one. The square root of 36 is 6, so species richness increases 6 times.

optionRationale.3: 36 would hold only if Z were 1.

questions.stem: In Paul Ehrlich's rivet popper hypothesis, the species in an ecosystem are compared to
options: the rivets that hold an airplane together
the roots of a banyan tree
questions.explanation: Ehrlich compared species with rivets in an airplane. Losing a few may not matter at first, but loss of more rivets weakens the structure, as the loss of species may weaken the ecosystem.

optionRationale.1: The comparison made was with rivets of an airplane.
optionRationale.2: The comparison made was with rivets of an airplane.
optionRationale.4: The comparison made was with rivets of an airplane.

questions.stem: A rare orchid grows naturally on a single hill in the Western Ghats and nowhere else in the world. Such a species is called
questions.explanation: A species confined to a particular region and found nowhere else is endemic. Endemism is typical of hotspots, and the narrow range makes endemic species very vulnerable to habitat loss.

optionRationale.2: An alien species is introduced from elsewhere.
optionRationale.3: A migratory species moves between regions seasonally.
optionRationale.4: The orchid still exists, so it is not extinct.

questions.stem: Match the scientist in List-I with the idea in List-II.
questions.explanation: Humboldt described the increase of species richness with area. Tilman's long-term experiments linked diversity to productivity and stability. Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis, and May estimated the number of species on earth at about seven million.

optionRationale.1: This pairs 'Alexander von Humboldt' with 'Long-term plot experiments on stability of communities', which describes 'David Tilman'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'Paul Ehrlich' with 'Global estimate of about 7 million species', which describes 'Robert May'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Alexander von Humboldt' with 'Rivet popper hypothesis', which describes 'Paul Ehrlich'.

questions.objective: Match scientists with their ideas on biodiversity

right: II. Long-term plot experiments on stability of communities
IV. Global estimate of about 7 million species

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Biodiversity hotspots deserve high priority in conservation.
Reason (R): Hotspots have very high species richness and high endemism, but they are threatened by habitat loss.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Hotspots are regions of very high species richness and endemism, and they are under threat from habitat destruction. Protecting them saves the greatest number of unique species per area, so R explains A.

optionRationale.2: R is the reason why hotspots are given priority.
optionRationale.4: A is true and R is true.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Habitat fragmentation badly affects animals that need large territories.
Reason (R): Habitat fragmentation always increases the area available to each species.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Fragmentation breaks large habitats into small patches, so mammals and birds that need large territories and migratory animals suffer. So A is true. Fragmentation reduces, not increases, the area available, so R is false.

optionRationale.1: R is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.2: R is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.stem: Match the extinct animal in List-I with its region in List-II.
questions.explanation: The dodo was a bird of Mauritius, the quagga a zebra-like animal of Africa, the thylacine a marsupial of Australia, and Steller's sea cow was found in Russian waters. All have become extinct in the last 500 years.

optionRationale.2: This pairs 'Thylacine' with 'Russia', which describes 'Steller's sea cow'.

questions.objective: Match extinct animals with their regions

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about biodiversity patterns.
A. Species diversity decreases from the equator towards the poles.
B. India has only about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area but about 8.1 per cent of its species diversity.
C. Species diversity is greater in temperate regions than in tropical regions.
D. The Amazonian rainforest has the greatest biodiversity on earth.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Diversity falls from the equator to the poles, and India holds a large share of the world's species for its area. The Amazon is the richest region on earth. Temperate regions have lower diversity than the tropics, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is also correct, so this option is incomplete.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.4: C is wrong, so not all four are correct.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the causes of biodiversity loss.
A. The 'evil quartet' includes habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions.
B. Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause of biodiversity loss.
C. The present rate of extinction is lower than that before the appearance of humans.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The evil quartet lists the four main causes, and habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important. The present rate of extinction is about 100 to 1000 times higher than the pre-human rate, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.1: C is wrong, since the present rate is much higher.
optionRationale.2: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, so not all three are correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on causes of biodiversity loss
